title: Liga MX
wiki_lead:
Liga MX, officially as Liga BBVA MX for sponsorship reasons, is a professional association football league in Mexico and the highest level of the Mexican football league system. The league is contested by 18 participating clubs, the season is divided into two tournaments: Apertura (from July to December) and Clausura (from January to May). The champions of each tournament are decided by a final knockout phase, commonly known as Liguilla. Since 2020, promotion and relegation has been suspended.
Formerly known as Liga Mayor (1943–1949), Campeonato de la Rama Profesional de la FMF (1949–1960) and Primera División Profesional de México (1960–2012). The league has been held in 115 editions, the inaugural season in the professional era was played in 1943–44 with Asturias crowned as the first champions.
Liga MX currently ranks first in CONCACAF's league ranking index. According to the IFFHS, it was ranked as the 10th strongest league in the first decade of the 21st century. According to CONCACAF, the league with an average attendance of 25,557 during the 2014–15 season, draws the largest crowds on average of any football league in the Americas.
Twenty-four clubs have been champions at least once. América is the most successful club with sixteen titles, Guadalajara and Toluca with twelve titles each, Cruz Azul with ten titles, Tigres UANL and León with eight titles each.

History


Precursor amateur leagues
Prior to the beginning of the Liga Mayor in the professional era of Mexican football, there was no national and professional league in Mexico, and all football competitions were held within relatively small geographical regions. In 1902, an amateur association of football supporters known as Asociación de Aficionados de México en la Liga de Football created the first amateur football league in Mexico known as Liga Mexicana de Football Amateur Association, a local league of clubs near and around Mexico City. The league was held from 1902 to 1920, and the inaugural season was contested by five clubs.
In 1920, a separatist league known as Liga Nacional was created by Real Club España, after its withdrawal from the Liga Mexicana in 1919. The league was held for two seasons (1920–21 and 1921–22), and the inaugural season was contested by five clubs.
The Liga Mexicana and the Liga Nacional are considered the two most relevant precursor amateur leagues, but not as direct predecessors of Liga MX. However, other regional and state leagues were also held in the country: Liga Amateur de Jalisco, Liga Amateur de Veracruz, Liga Amateur de Puebla, Liga Amateur del Bajío, Liga Amateur de Hidalgo and Liga Amateur Mexiquense.
